selected_source.provider: Hear The Boat Sing Blogspot archive / American Cinematographer caption reprint
selected_source.caption: A group of blue-clad Oompa-Loompas, all played by Deep Roy and further miniaturized and multiplied digitally, man the oars on the seahorse-shaped galley traversing the Chocolate River.

performance_mechanism.binding: Warner Bros. production notes state that Deep Roy supplied the entire Oompa-Loompa community, performing each visible Oompa separately, including all twenty when a scene required twenty bodies.

production.binding: AFI fixes the retained performance to Tim Burton's 2005 Warner Bros. feature, released July 15, 2005.

multiplicity_boundary.mechanism: Separate Deep Roy performances were miniaturized, composited, and multiplied to author the Oompa-Loompa population.
multiplicity_boundary.prohibited_inference: The packet does not treat one isolated Oompa Loompa as sufficient evidence for the collective role.

candidate.recipe: auto-orient; Lanczos cover-resize to 1534x1200; east extent to 1260x1000; strip metadata; JPEG quality 94

crop_preview.semantics: The wall simulation removes seven pixels from each outside edge while preserving the synchronized blue-clad rowers, their oars, the passenger scale, galley and Chocolate River.

rejected_orbit_summary: The 1971 film boat, book illustrations, production sketches, stage versions, advertising mascots, toys, cosplay, posters and untransformed Deep Roy were rejected.

notes: The selected 2005 Chocolate River frame presents a synchronized group of blue-clad Oompa Loompas rather than an isolated worker, so the card displays the authored collective role.

The caption identifies every visible Oompa as a Deep Roy performance that was miniaturized and multiplied digitally; Warner Bros. independently states that Roy supplied the entire community and performed each visible body separately.

The 120-percent east-anchored enlargement preserves the repeated rowing bodies, synchronized oars, passenger scale, pink galley and Chocolate River while making the many-body mechanism legible at card size.
The 1246x1000 wall simulation removes seven pixels from each outside edge without changing the repeated-body count, collective-role identity or production-context ruling.
